post.title: Nobody is watching you as much as you think. 👁️
post.description:
Send this to someone who overthinks what others think.

In a 2000 Cornell study, students wearing an embarrassing T-shirt guessed about half the room noticed. Only about a quarter did.
post.pinned_comment: What would you do if nobody was watching? 👇

scenes.narration: Nobody is watching you. Not the way you think they are.
In the year 2000, researchers at Cornell asked students to walk into a room wearing an embarrassing T-shirt.
The students guessed that about half the people in the room would notice it.
The real number? Only about one in four.
Psychologists call it the spotlight effect. We feel like a bright light follows us everywhere.
But everyone else is standing in their own spotlight, too busy worrying about themselves.
That awkward thing you said last week? Most people forgot it the same day.
So stop letting imaginary eyes make your decisions.
Start the channel. Go to the gym. Ask the question. Wear the shirt.
The fear of being seen is louder than the people actually looking.
Nobody is watching closely. That is not lonely. That is freedom.
So what would you do today, if nobody was watching?
